references.text: Moses reminds the people to fear the Lord and teach their children, which is the same theme of reverence for God and instruction of future generations.
The Lord expresses his desire that the people should fear him and keep all his commandments, so that it may go well with them.
The promise of long days in the land is tied to keeping the Lord's commandments and statutes.
The promise of living long is connected to honoring parents and keeping the Lord's commandments.
The promise of extended days in the land is conditioned on obedience to the Lord's commands.
Fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, reflecting the call to reverence for God in Deuteronomy.
Fear of the Lord leads to wisdom and long life.
The conclusion about humanity's duty: Fear God and keep his commandments, summarizing the message of Deuteronomy 6:2.
The command to honor parents with a promise of long days, as reflected in the promise of extended life.
The instruction to fear God and keep his commandments.
Paul quotes the promise of long days connected to honoring parents, which is linked to the commands in Deuteronomy.
